text:
QUOTE: "`mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init(buf, len)` (`memory_buffer_alloc.c:566`) carves allocations out of a caller-supplied buffer. It calls `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` to point the hooks at its own functions."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the built-in buffer allocator's init function calls the runtime setter to install itself over the pointers, and that it is the only internal caller ("the only internal caller is the built-in allocator below"). It does not name MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C, but the mechanism and location are clear.
